headline: High: shared file/clipboard and MCP/browser surfaces make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A reads files, clipboard, screen capture, and supported app content by default; Agent B uses browsers and MCP, so content from A can be bridged into B through shared files or copy/paste. No provenance tracking is documented for either side, so injected instructions in documents or diagrams are plausible. The interaction is inferred from both profiles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF Agent A content is copied into Agent B prompts or MCP inputs, injected instructions can steer B.
IF both agents access the same workspace or clipboard, untrusted file text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable clipboard bridging between the agents.
Use a read-only handoff file format with explicit provenance labels.
Strip instructions from imported documents before B processes them.
requires-engineering: add provenance filtering at the orchestrator boundary.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents into separate workspaces.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while Agent B handles PDFs, text, images, and diagram XML and can send data to broad external APIs. If they share a workspace or hand off files, sensitive content from A can flow into B and then out to third-party model endpoints. This is a plausible default-path risk, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF A receives uploaded files or screenshots containing sensitive data and B processes the same files, leakage is possible.
IF B forwards document contents to external APIs, any data from A in those files can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Avoid passing sensitive files from A to B.
Redact screenshots and PDFs before B ingests them.
Use separate accounts or workspaces for each agent.
Turn off B processing for confidential documents.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention checks on handoff files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has read-only filesystem access and no git or shell writes, while B has broad network egress, browser access, and MCP. They do not obviously contend on the same mutable local resource, but B can still mutate remote or MCP-backed state while A reads local content that may be reused. Because shared locking is undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF B writes to an MCP-backed or remote resource that A also reads, stale or conflicting state can occur.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable workspace, write conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces or repositories.
Disable concurrent edits to shared diagrams.
Use explicit file-locking or check-in/check-out for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add conflict detection for remote/MCP writes.
requires-engineering: serialize edits through a single coordinator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce file-derived summaries and app-context outputs, and B is a document-processing agent that may treat those outputs as input for diagram generation or other actions. That creates a plausible chain where A's output is accepted without verification by B. The profiles do not prove automation, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF B consumes A's summaries as authoritative source text, errors can cascade into generated diagrams or documents.
IF A's extracted app context is forwarded to B without verification, B may act on hallucinated or stale facts.
mitigations: Require B to cite original source files, not A's summaries.
Add a human review step before B acts on A's output.
Compare A's output against the source document for key facts.
Use a template that separates extracted facts from interpretations.
requires-engineering: implement automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: A is a closed-source desktop app handling uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code; B is open-source but sends content to multiple external AI providers and handles API keys. If regulated or residency-bound data enters A and then B, retention and jurisdiction mismatches are plausible. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency controls, so uncertainty warrants medium.
conditions: IF EU PII or other regulated data is processed by both agents, residency and retention obligations may diverge.
IF B forwards content to non-approved external providers, compliance controls can be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Route only de-identified content to B.
Review vendor DPAs and retention settings before use.
Separate secrets from documents processed by B.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for regulated data.
